items.title: Pay advance payment (Abschlag)
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den fälligen Abschlag von 214,00 € bis spätestens 11.09.2026.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date, 11.09.2026, as the payment deadline. A calendar date printed in a letter is used as written and is not recalculated from a delivery-fiction or statutory period. Note: this date already lies in the past relative to today (2026-09-25), and the entire letter shows strong hallmarks of a bank-detail-change payment scam (see warnings) — the payment should not be made to the account given.

warnings: This letter shows the classic pattern of a bank-account-change payment scam: it demands an urgent payment to a 'new' account allegedly due to a payment-system changeover, with a threat to cut off electricity without further notice if payment is not made within days.

The account holder given for the 'new' IBAN is 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.' — a completely different, foreign-sounding company name (s.r.o. is a Czech/Slovak legal form), not 'Stadtwerke Musterstadt'; a genuine utility would never route payments through an unrelated third-party company.

The letter explicitly instructs the recipient not to reply to the letter and to call only a given mobile phone number (015x) instead of the utility's normal, verifiable contact channels — a typical tactic to prevent the recipient from checking the change through official means.
The sender's email address uses the placeholder/example domain 'kundenservice-mail.example', which is not a real, verifiable company domain.

The very short deadline (only a few days) combined with the threat of immediate service disconnection is a pressure tactic typical of scam letters and is not how German utilities normally handle a genuine bank-detail change (which is usually announced with adequate notice and without threats).

Recommendation: do not transfer money to the IBAN given in this letter; contact Stadtwerke Musterstadt directly using contact details from a trusted source (e.g. a previous bill or the official website) to verify before paying anything.
